questions.scenario: A developer must process items from an SQS queue in batches of 10 with a Lambda function, and a single failed item should not cause the whole batch to be reprocessed. What should be configured?
options: ReportBatchItemFailures in the event source mapping response
questions.explain: With partial batch response (ReportBatchItemFailures) the function returns the identifiers of only the items that failed, so SQS makes just those visible again while successful items are deleted. Without it, one failure causes the entire batch to be retried. Batch size, visibility timeout and concurrency do not provide item-level failure handling.

questions.scenario: An application must return the 20 most recent orders for a customer, sorted newest first, from a DynamoDB table with partition key customer_id and sort key order_date. Which Query parameters achieve this efficiently?
options: Limit 20 with ScanIndexForward set to false
Scan with a FilterExpression and sort in the application
Limit 20 with ScanIndexForward set to true
Query all items and slice the result in code
questions.explain: ScanIndexForward set to false reverses the sort key order so the newest items come first, and Limit 20 stops after reading 20 items — a minimal, cheap read. Setting it to true returns oldest first. Scanning or reading everything then slicing in code consumes capacity for data you discard.

questions.scenario: An application must invoke a Lambda function when a file lands in S3, but only for objects with the prefix incoming/ and suffix .csv. How should this be configured?
options: An S3 event notification with prefix and suffix filters
A Lambda function that lists the bucket every minute
A CloudTrail trail with an EventBridge rule on every S3 API call
questions.explain: S3 event notifications support prefix and suffix filters natively, so only matching objects invoke the function and nothing else is charged for. Polling wastes invocations and adds latency. A CloudTrail-driven rule would fire on all API activity and requires extra filtering. Lifecycle rules manage storage class and expiry.

questions.scenario: A team must run a workflow where five tasks execute simultaneously and the workflow continues only when all have finished. Which Step Functions state should be used?
questions.explain: A Parallel state runs multiple branches concurrently and waits for every branch to complete before moving on. Choice adds conditional branching, Wait delays for a duration or until a timestamp, and Pass simply passes data through, optionally transforming it.

questions.scenario: Which TWO approaches reduce the cold start time of an AWS Lambda function?
options: Reduce the size of the deployment package and its dependencies
Use provisioned concurrency on the alias
Attach the function to a VPC
questions.explain: Smaller packages load faster during initialisation, and provisioned concurrency keeps environments initialised so requests never experience a cold start. Increasing the timeout does not affect startup. Attaching to a VPC historically increased cold start time. Environment variables have no meaningful effect on initialisation speed.

questions.scenario: An application requires a message to be delivered to a queue only after a 10-minute delay. Which SQS feature provides this?
options: A message timer or queue delivery delay of up to 15 minutes
questions.explain: SQS supports delay queues and per-message timers of up to 15 minutes, during which a message stays invisible to consumers. Visibility timeout hides a message after it has been received. Long polling controls how receive calls wait, and dead-letter queues capture repeatedly failing messages.

questions.scenario: Which API operation should a developer use to write up to 25 items to DynamoDB in a single call?
questions.explain: BatchWriteItem writes up to 25 items (or 16 MB) per call, reducing round trips, though individual items may fail and must be retried via UnprocessedItems. TransactWriteItems is atomic but limited to 100 items with higher cost. Looping PutItem multiplies network calls, and UpdateItem modifies a single item.

questions.scenario: An application must expose a WebSocket API so a server can push updates to connected clients. Which service supports this natively?
questions.explain: API Gateway WebSocket APIs maintain persistent bidirectional connections and manage connection IDs so the backend can push messages to clients. REST APIs are request/response only. CloudFront is a CDN, and SQS is a queue that clients cannot subscribe to directly.

questions.scenario: A Lambda function must access a value that differs between the dev, test and prod deployments without changing code. What is the simplest mechanism?
options: Environment variables set per function configuration
Hard-coded constants with an if statement
A separate code repository per environment
questions.explain: Environment variables externalise configuration so the same code artifact behaves differently per deployment, which is the standard twelve-factor approach. Hard-coded branching requires code changes and redeployment for every environment tweak, separate repositories duplicate maintenance, and runtimes are unrelated to configuration.

questions.scenario: Which DynamoDB feature allows an application to write an item only if it does not already exist?
options: A condition expression using attribute_not_exists on the key
questions.explain: A conditional write with attribute_not_exists on the partition key succeeds only when no item with that key exists, and otherwise raises ConditionalCheckFailedException — the standard way to implement create-if-absent semantics. Indexes serve query patterns, TTL deletes expired items, and Streams report changes.

questions.scenario: An application processes images and needs temporary disk space of about 2 GB during processing in a Lambda function. What must be configured?
options: Increase the ephemeral storage (/tmp) allocation up to 10,240 MB
Attach an EBS volume to the function
questions.explain: Lambda's /tmp ephemeral storage is configurable from 512 MB to 10,240 MB, which covers a 2 GB working set. Lambda cannot attach EBS volumes. The deployment package limit governs code size, not runtime scratch space, and layers ship read-only dependencies.

questions.scenario: Which service should be used to deliver streaming data to Amazon S3 with automatic buffering, compression and no consumer code to manage?
questions.explain: Firehose is a fully managed delivery stream that buffers, optionally transforms and compresses records, then writes them to destinations such as S3 with no consumer application to build or scale. Kinesis Data Streams requires you to write and operate consumers. SQS is a queue, and Glue is an ETL service.

questions.scenario: An application must retry a failed AWS SDK call in a way that avoids overwhelming the service when many clients fail simultaneously. What should be used?
options: Immediate retry in a tight loop
A fixed 1-second retry interval for all clients
questions.explain: Exponential backoff increases the wait between attempts, and jitter randomises it so clients do not synchronise into repeated thundering herds. Tight loops and fixed intervals cause exactly that synchronisation, and abandoning retries entirely fails requests that would have succeeded moments later.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure ordering of records for a specific user in Kinesis Data Streams while maximising overall throughput. What should be used as the partition key?
questions.explain: Using the user ID hashes all of that user's records to the same shard, preserving order for that user while different users spread across shards for parallel throughput. A random UUID destroys per-user ordering, a constant sends everything to one shard creating a bottleneck, and timestamps cluster writes on the hot shard.

questions.scenario: Which statement about API Gateway usage plans and API keys is correct?
options: They meter and throttle requests per client but are not a secure authentication mechanism
questions.explain: API keys identify a caller so a usage plan can apply per-client rate limits and quotas, but keys are transmitted as a header and are not a security control — AWS explicitly recommends pairing them with real authorisation. They do not encrypt payloads, replace IAM, or authenticate end users.

questions.scenario: An application must store objects that must not be deleted or overwritten for seven years to satisfy regulation. Which S3 feature enforces this?
options: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
questions.explain: Object Lock in compliance mode enforces write-once-read-many retention that not even the root user can shorten or bypass until the period expires. Versioning preserves prior versions but permits deletion, lifecycle rules move or expire data, and Intelligent-Tiering optimises storage cost by access pattern.

questions.scenario: Which approach lets a Lambda function process a 5 GB file stored in S3 without loading it entirely into memory?
options: Read the object in ranges using byte-range requests and process incrementally
Increase Lambda memory to 10,240 MB and load it all
Copy the object into an environment variable
Store the file in a Lambda layer
questions.explain: S3 supports byte-range GET requests, so a function can stream and process chunks sequentially with modest memory. Even the maximum 10,240 MB cannot comfortably hold a 5 GB file plus runtime overhead. Environment variables are limited to 4 KB and layers are capped well below 5 GB.

questions.scenario: A team wants to reduce DynamoDB costs for a table where only 5 percent of items are read regularly. Which change is MOST effective?
options: Add a caching layer for the hot items
Convert all reads to strongly consistent
Add three more global secondary indexes
questions.explain: Caching the small hot subset eliminates most repeated reads, reducing consumed capacity and cost directly. Raising capacity increases spend, strongly consistent reads double RCU consumption, and extra GSIs add storage and write cost without reducing read cost.

questions.scenario: Which event source invokes a Lambda function synchronously?
questions.explain: API Gateway invokes Lambda synchronously and waits for the response to return to the client, which is why errors surface immediately and Lambda performs no automatic retries. S3, SNS and EventBridge all invoke asynchronously, where Lambda retries twice before sending the event to a destination or dead-letter queue.

questions.scenario: A developer must ensure that two Lambda functions triggered by the same SNS topic both receive every message even if one function is temporarily failing. What should be added?
options: An SQS queue between SNS and each function
A shorter SNS delivery retry policy
A single shared SQS queue for both functions
API Gateway in front of the functions
questions.explain: SNS delivers to Lambda asynchronously and eventually gives up on a persistently failing subscriber, losing the message. Placing an SQS queue per function durably stores messages so each function can recover and catch up independently. A single shared queue would let only one function consume each message.

questions.scenario: Which service provides a managed GraphQL API with real-time subscriptions and direct data source integration?
questions.explain: AppSync is a managed GraphQL service supporting queries, mutations and real-time subscriptions, with resolvers that connect directly to DynamoDB, Lambda, RDS and OpenSearch. API Gateway REST APIs are not GraphQL, Amplify Hosting serves front-end applications, and CloudFront is a CDN.

questions.scenario: Which IAM policy element specifies WHO is allowed to perform an action in a resource-based policy?
questions.explain: The Principal element names the identity being granted or denied access and appears only in resource-based policies, because identity-based policies are already attached to a principal. Action lists operations, Resource lists targets, and Condition adds contextual constraints.

questions.scenario: An application must allow users to access only their own records in an S3 bucket organised as /users/{user_id}/. Which approach scales to millions of users?
options: An IAM role with a policy variable such as ${aws:userid} or a Cognito identity substitution in the resource ARN
An IAM user and policy per customer
A public bucket with obscure key names
questions.explain: Policy variables substitute the authenticated identity into the resource ARN at evaluation time, so a single role scopes every user to their own prefix. Creating an IAM user or bucket per customer hits hard account limits and is unmanageable at scale. Obscure names in a public bucket is security through obscurity.

questions.scenario: Which action should be taken if an IAM access key is accidentally committed to a public repository?
options: Immediately deactivate and delete the key, rotate credentials, and review CloudTrail for misuse
Rename the repository to private and keep the key
Add the key to .gitignore going forward
Wait to see whether the key is used
questions.explain: An exposed key must be assumed compromised immediately: deactivate and delete it, issue replacements, and audit CloudTrail for unauthorised activity. Making the repository private does not undo exposure because the key is already in history and likely scraped. Ignoring the file going forward and waiting both leave an active credential in attackers' hands.

questions.scenario: Which service can automatically detect sensitive data such as PII stored in Amazon S3 buckets?
questions.explain: Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII and financial information in S3, and reports on bucket security posture. Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities, Shield protects against DDoS, and GuardDuty detects malicious account and network activity.

questions.scenario: Which TWO statements about AWS KMS key policies and IAM policies are correct?
options: A KMS key policy is required; without it the key cannot be managed
IAM policies alone cannot grant access to a KMS key unless the key policy delegates to IAM
IAM policies always override key policies
Key policies apply only to symmetric keys
Key policies cannot reference other AWS accounts
questions.explain: Every KMS key has a key policy and it is the primary access control; if it does not delegate permission management to IAM (typically by allowing the account root principal), IAM policies cannot grant access to that key. Key policies never lose to IAM, apply to both symmetric and asymmetric keys, and can grant access to other accounts.

questions.scenario: An application must validate that an incoming request originated from Amazon SNS and was not forged. What should be done?
options: Verify the message signature using the certificate referenced by SigningCertURL
Check that the request contains a Message field
Trust any request to the endpoint
Compare the source IP to a hard-coded list
questions.explain: SNS signs every message, and subscribers should download the certificate from the SigningCertURL (validating it is an Amazon domain) and verify the signature before acting. Checking for a field or trusting the endpoint allows trivial forgery, and SNS source IPs are dynamic so hard-coded lists break.

questions.scenario: Which encryption option should be used when a company must control the key material, audit every use, and allow other AWS accounts to decrypt?
options: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key and a key policy granting the other account
Client-side encryption with a key in application code
No encryption with a restrictive bucket policy
questions.explain: A customer managed KMS key gives full control over rotation and policy, logs every operation to CloudTrail for auditing, and its key policy can grant decrypt permission to another account. SSE-S3 offers no key control or cross-account grants. Embedding a key in application code is a leak waiting to happen, and a bucket policy alone provides no encryption.

questions.scenario: What is the correct way for an application to handle an ExpiredTokenException from AWS STS?
options: Obtain fresh temporary credentials by assuming the role again
Retry the same request with the same credentials indefinitely
questions.explain: Temporary credentials expire by design, so the correct response is to request new ones, which AWS SDKs typically do automatically for role-based providers. Retrying with expired credentials always fails, moving to permanent keys reintroduces long-lived secrets, and ignoring the error leaves the call unperformed.

questions.scenario: Which statement about Amazon Cognito user pool tokens is correct?
options: The ID token contains user identity claims and the access token authorises API calls
Both tokens are opaque strings with no claims
The refresh token should be sent with every API request
questions.explain: A user pool issues an ID token carrying identity claims about the user, an access token used to authorise API access with scopes, and a refresh token used solely to obtain new tokens. All are JWTs with readable claims, ID and access tokens expire (commonly after one hour), and the refresh token must be stored securely rather than sent on every request.

questions.scenario: A Lambda function must be prevented from being invoked by any principal except a specific API Gateway API. What should be configured?
options: A Lambda resource-based policy naming the API Gateway service and source ARN
questions.explain: A Lambda resource-based policy grants lambda:InvokeFunction to a specific principal, and the SourceArn condition restricts it to one API, which is exactly what API Gateway integrations create. Timeouts, VPC endpoints and concurrency limits control execution and networking, not who may invoke.

questions.scenario: Which practice best protects an application against injection attacks when building database queries?
options: Use parameterised queries or prepared statements
Concatenate user input into the query string
questions.explain: Parameterised queries send the query structure and the data separately so user input is never interpreted as code, which eliminates injection regardless of the input. String concatenation is the vulnerability itself, escaping only some characters misses many vectors, and client-side validation is trivially bypassed.

questions.scenario: Which AWS feature should be used to give a Lambda function access to a secret without embedding the retrieval code in every function?
options: The AWS Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension
A hard-coded value in the handler
An environment variable containing the plaintext secret
questions.explain: The Parameters and Secrets Lambda Extension retrieves and caches values from Secrets Manager and Parameter Store via a local HTTP endpoint, reducing both code duplication and API calls. Hard-coded values and plaintext environment variables expose secrets, and a public S3 object exposes them to the world.

questions.scenario: An application must ensure that data stored in an Amazon RDS database is encrypted at rest. When must encryption be enabled?
options: At database creation, or by restoring a snapshot into a new encrypted instance
At any time with a single toggle on the running instance
It is always enabled and cannot be configured
questions.explain: RDS encryption at rest must be chosen when the instance is created; an existing unencrypted instance cannot simply be toggled. The supported path is to snapshot it, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, and restore into a new encrypted instance. Application-level encryption is a separate additional measure.

questions.scenario: Which CloudTrail feature helps detect whether a specific S3 object was read by an unauthorised principal?
options: Data events for S3 object-level operations
questions.explain: CloudTrail data events record object-level operations such as GetObject and PutObject, which is what identifies who read a particular object. Management events cover control-plane actions like bucket creation but not object reads. Dashboards visualise metrics, and Config tracks configuration compliance.

questions.scenario: Which statement about the principle of least privilege is correct in the context of an IAM role for a Lambda function?
options: The role should grant only the specific actions and resources the function actually uses
The role should grant full access to simplify development
The role should be shared across all functions in the account
The role should include an explicit allow for all IAM actions
questions.explain: Least privilege means granting exactly the actions on exactly the resources required, so a compromised function has minimal reach. Full access, shared roles across unrelated functions, and blanket IAM permissions all expand the blast radius of any compromise or bug.

questions.scenario: An application uses presigned S3 URLs for downloads. What limits how long the URL remains valid?
options: The expiration set when generating the URL, bounded by the signing credentials' own lifetime
questions.explain: A presigned URL carries an explicit expiration, but it also stops working if the credentials that signed it expire first — which matters when signing with temporary role credentials that may last only an hour. Lifecycle policies, storage classes and CDN TTLs do not govern presigned URL validity.

questions.scenario: Which approach prevents an attacker who obtains a database read replica endpoint from reading data directly?
options: Place the database in private subnets with security groups restricting access to the application tier
Use a longer database password only
questions.explain: Network isolation through private subnets and security groups that permit traffic only from the application's security group means the endpoint is unreachable from the internet at all, so knowing it is useless. Renaming is obscurity, a strong password still allows connection attempts, and backups protect durability rather than access.

questions.scenario: Which CodeDeploy deployment type is required to deploy to AWS Lambda?
questions.explain: Lambda deployments in CodeDeploy always use blue/green traffic shifting between two versions behind an alias, with canary, linear or all-at-once configurations. In-place deployment applies to EC2 and on-premises instances, while rolling with additional batch and immutable are Elastic Beanstalk policies.

questions.scenario: A developer must reference a parameter value supplied at stack creation inside a CloudFormation resource property. Which intrinsic function is used?
questions.explain: Ref returns the value of a parameter, or the physical ID of a resource, and is the standard way to consume a parameter in a property. Fn::GetAtt retrieves a specific attribute of a created resource, and Fn::Join and Fn::Sub build composite strings, though Fn::Sub can also interpolate parameters.

questions.scenario: Which statement about CodePipeline stage transitions is correct?
options: A stage runs only if the previous stage succeeded, and transitions can be disabled manually
A failed stage is skipped automatically
questions.explain: CodePipeline stages execute sequentially and only proceed when the preceding stage succeeds; transitions can also be disabled to hold a release. Stages do not run in parallel (though actions within a stage can), failures stop the pipeline rather than retrying forever, and a failed stage is never silently skipped.

questions.scenario: A SAM template must define an API endpoint that triggers a function on POST /orders. Where is this defined?
options: In the function's Events property with an Api event type
In a separate CodeDeploy appspec file
questions.explain: SAM functions declare an Events property; an Api event with a path and method automatically creates the API Gateway route, integration and invoke permission. appspec.yml governs CodeDeploy deployments, buildspec.yml governs CodeBuild, and .ebextensions configures Elastic Beanstalk.

questions.scenario: Which approach ensures a container image used in production is immutable and traceable to a specific build?
options: Tag images with a unique build identifier or digest rather than only 'latest'
Rebuild the image on every container start
Store images in an S3 bucket
questions.explain: Unique tags or image digests pin a deployment to an exact artifact, making rollbacks and audits reliable. The latest tag is mutable, so the same reference can resolve to different images over time. Rebuilding at start time is slow and non-deterministic, and S3 is not a container registry.

questions.scenario: A CloudFormation update must not proceed if a resource would be replaced. What should the developer do?
options: Create a change set and inspect the Replacement column before executing
Execute the update and monitor events
questions.explain: A change set lists each change with a Replacement indicator showing whether a resource will be recreated, allowing the update to be abandoned before any action is taken. Executing and watching means the replacement has already begun, deleting the stack destroys everything, and disabling rollback removes the safety net.

questions.scenario: Which TWO are benefits of using infrastructure as code with CloudFormation or SAM?
options: Environments can be recreated consistently from version-controlled templates
Failed updates roll back automatically to the previous state
It removes the need for IAM permissions
It eliminates the need for testing
questions.explain: Templates in version control make environments reproducible and reviewable, and CloudFormation rolls back automatically when an update fails, avoiding half-applied changes. IAM permissions are still required (indeed CloudFormation acts with them), resources still cost money, and testing remains essential.

questions.scenario: An Elastic Beanstalk application must swap environments to release a new version with instant rollback. Which feature provides this?
options: Swap environment URLs (CNAME swap) between two environments
questions.explain: Deploying to a second environment and swapping CNAMEs is Elastic Beanstalk's blue/green mechanism, and rollback is simply swapping back. Terminating and recreating causes downtime, rolling updates instances in place with no instant rollback, and instance type changes are unrelated to release strategy.

questions.scenario: Which CodeBuild feature allows reuse of downloaded dependencies between builds to reduce build time?
options: Caching, for example local or S3 cache of dependency directories
questions.explain: CodeBuild supports S3 and local caching of specified paths such as node_modules or a package manager cache, so subsequent builds skip re-downloading dependencies. Larger compute speeds execution without avoiding downloads, skipping the install phase breaks the build, and artifact bucket size is irrelevant.

questions.scenario: A team must deploy the same Lambda function to three regions for latency and resilience. Which approach is MOST maintainable?
options: A single template deployed by CloudFormation StackSets to all three regions
Manually zipping and uploading in each region
A single region with global replication of Lambda
questions.explain: StackSets deploy one template across regions and keep them synchronised on every change. Manual uploads and divergent templates drift immediately and are error-prone. Lambda functions are regional resources and there is no automatic global replication of them.

questions.scenario: Which file defines the container definitions, CPU and memory for an Amazon ECS deployment?
questions.explain: An ECS task definition specifies container images, CPU and memory reservations, port mappings, environment variables and IAM roles. buildspec.yml drives CodeBuild, appspec.yml drives CodeDeploy (including which task definition to deploy), and .ebextensions configures Elastic Beanstalk.

questions.scenario: What is the purpose of the AWS SAM 'sam sync' command during development?
options: It rapidly updates code and infrastructure in a development stack for fast iteration
It creates a change set for production only
questions.explain: sam sync shortens the inner development loop by pushing code changes directly and applying template changes quickly to a development stack, avoiding a full package-and-deploy cycle. It is explicitly not intended for production. It neither deletes stacks nor manages credentials.

questions.scenario: A pipeline deploys to production only after a successful deployment to staging. How should this be modelled in CodePipeline?
options: Two sequential deploy stages, staging then production, optionally with a manual approval between
One stage with both deployments in parallel
A single deploy action targeting both environments
questions.explain: Sequential stages enforce that production runs only after staging succeeds, and a manual approval action between them adds a human gate. Parallel actions or simultaneous pipelines remove the dependency entirely, and one action cannot meaningfully target two environments with a gate between them.

questions.scenario: Which CloudFormation resource attribute ensures one resource is created only after another completes?
questions.explain: DependsOn explicitly orders resource creation when CloudFormation cannot infer the dependency from a Ref or Fn::GetAtt. Metadata attaches arbitrary information, DeletionPolicy controls behaviour on stack deletion, and Condition controls whether a resource is created at all.

questions.scenario: A developer needs the fastest possible deployment for a development environment where brief downtime is acceptable. Which Elastic Beanstalk policy should be chosen?
questions.explain: All at once updates every instance simultaneously, making it the fastest and cheapest option, with brief downtime that is acceptable in development. Immutable and blue/green prioritise safety at extra cost and time, and rolling with additional batch is slower because it proceeds in batches.

questions.scenario: A developer must find which API call failed and why in a distributed application, including the exact error message returned by DynamoDB. Where should they look?
options: The X-Ray trace subsegment for the DynamoDB call, plus the function's CloudWatch logs
questions.explain: X-Ray subsegments record downstream AWS SDK calls with error and fault flags and exception details, and the function's CloudWatch logs capture the full message and stack trace. Flow Logs show network traffic without application context, and S3 access logs and Route 53 health checks are unrelated to DynamoDB errors.

questions.scenario: Which CloudWatch Logs feature streams log events to a Lambda function or Kinesis stream in near real time?
questions.explain: Subscription filters deliver matching log events in near real time to destinations such as Lambda, Kinesis Data Streams or Firehose, enabling custom processing pipelines. Metric filters produce numeric metrics instead, retention governs how long data is kept, and dashboards display existing data.

questions.scenario: An application's p99 latency spikes only during deployments. Which is the MOST likely cause for a Lambda-based application?
options: Cold starts on new versions as fresh execution environments initialise
questions.explain: Publishing a new version invalidates warm environments, so early requests after a deployment pay initialisation cost and tail latency rises. Provisioned concurrency with a pre-traffic hook mitigates it. Log retention, alarm counts and bucket size have no effect on request latency.

questions.scenario: Which metric indicates that an Amazon SQS queue is accumulating unprocessed work?
questions.explain: A rising count of visible messages means producers are outpacing consumers and backlog is growing; ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage rising confirms it. Empty receives indicate consumers polling an idle queue, message size relates to payloads, and a falling oldest-message age means the backlog is clearing.

questions.scenario: A developer wants to see aggregated latency percentiles for an API Gateway stage. What should be enabled?
options: Detailed CloudWatch metrics for the stage
questions.explain: Enabling detailed metrics publishes per-method CloudWatch metrics including Latency and IntegrationLatency, which support percentile statistics. Access logging records individual requests rather than aggregated percentiles, tracing every request is expensive and unnecessary for aggregates, and usage plans manage throttling and quotas.

questions.scenario: An application reads from a DynamoDB global secondary index and occasionally sees data that is slightly out of date. What explains this?
options: GSIs are eventually consistent and are updated asynchronously after the base table write
questions.explain: Writes propagate to a GSI asynchronously, so a read immediately after a write may not reflect it — GSIs never support strongly consistent reads. Index storage grows automatically, strongly consistent reads cannot even be requested on a GSI, and capacity mode does not affect propagation semantics.

questions.scenario: Which approach BEST reduces the latency of an API that performs several independent downstream calls?
options: Execute the independent calls concurrently rather than sequentially
questions.explain: When calls do not depend on one another, running them concurrently makes total latency approach the slowest single call rather than the sum of all. Raising the timeout tolerates slowness rather than reducing it, and alarms and retention are observability settings with no effect on latency.

questions.scenario: A Lambda function occasionally fails with an out-of-memory error. Which CloudWatch data confirms this?
options: The REPORT line in the function's logs showing Max Memory Used at or near the configured limit
questions.explain: Every invocation writes a REPORT line including Memory Size and Max Memory Used, so a value at the limit confirms memory exhaustion and indicates the allocation should be raised. Invocations counts calls, ConcurrentExecutions shows parallelism, and Throttles indicates concurrency limits rather than memory.

questions.scenario: Which action reduces the cost of storing infrequently queried application logs long term while keeping them available for audit?
options: Export or stream logs to Amazon S3 with lifecycle transitions to cheaper storage classes
Keep all logs in CloudWatch Logs indefinitely
Delete all logs after one day
Increase the CloudWatch Logs ingestion rate
questions.explain: CloudWatch Logs storage is comparatively expensive for long retention, so exporting or streaming to S3 and transitioning to Standard-IA or Glacier greatly reduces cost while preserving auditability. Indefinite CloudWatch retention is the expensive default, deleting after a day breaks audit requirements, and ingestion rate is not a retention cost lever.

questions.scenario: An application must alert on-call staff when a critical alarm fires. Which combination should be used?
options: A CloudWatch alarm with an SNS topic subscribed by email, SMS or a paging integration
questions.explain: Alarms publish state changes to an SNS topic, which fans out to email, SMS, HTTPS endpoints or paging tools such as PagerDuty. A dashboard requires someone to be watching, and S3 notifications and DynamoDB streams react to data events rather than metric thresholds.

questions.scenario: Which CloudWatch capability allows creating a metric from structured log data without a separate PutMetricData call?
questions.explain: EMF embeds metric definitions inside a structured JSON log entry, so CloudWatch extracts metrics automatically from logs the application already writes — avoiding extra API calls and their latency. Tags and stream names are organisational metadata, and alarm actions respond to threshold breaches.

questions.scenario: A developer needs to identify which specific database query in a request is slow. What should be added to the X-Ray instrumentation?
options: Custom subsegments around each query, with annotations identifying the query type
Only a single segment for the whole function
Metadata with the full result set
A higher sampling rate with no instrumentation
questions.explain: Wrapping each query in its own subsegment attributes time precisely, and annotations make those subsegments filterable because annotations are indexed. A single segment hides internal breakdown, storing full result sets in metadata bloats traces without aiding timing, and raising sampling without instrumentation produces more traces at the same low detail.
